source.title: Feature Geometry of LoRA Adapters: A Sparse Autoencoder Analysis of Representational Divergence in Fine-Tuned Language Models

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE-based feature analysis to LoRA-fine-tuned Gemma-2-9B and reports whether pretrained and adapter-specific dictionaries capture adapter-induced activations. This extends feature-recovery analysis to LoRA-induced representations in an LLM; it does not test the original toy-model setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports reconstruction errors, feature activation fractions, cosine similarities, principal angles, and CKA. Training losses and hyperparameter-selection results are not cataloged as claim results. The rows below prioritize all rank-by-layer reconstruction results in Tables 5 and 6, plus the reported weakly aligned fractions at the three layers shown in Table 8. Other Table 8 measures and geometric analyses are not included because of the 60-row limit.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs as a tool to analyse LoRA activation deltas in Gemma-2-9B. It reports its own delta-SAE method against Gemma Scope, plus geometric divergence between adapter and base dictionaries. Nothing measures whether the model's activations are superposed or whether a dictionary recovers the model's own features. Applying base-model Gemma Scope SAEs to off-distribution difference vectors (h∆) tests no version's claim. V5 completeness is about a model's own activations, not adapter deltas from another model.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that LoRA adapters induce feature structure geometrically separated from Gemma Scope features. The evidence is near-random cosine (0.071), principal angles near 74°, and low CKA at middle layers. Delta SAEs cut reconstruction error by 46–86%. They frame this as a monitoring gap. They note that no base-base SAE baseline exists and that the adapters left outputs unchanged.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LoRA fine-tuning, activation-delta SAEs, dictionary reconstruction and geometric comparisons in Gemma-2-9B, rather than toy networks designed to test superposition. It analyzes adapter-induced representations, not the original toy-model intervention or measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with layer and, for some measures, LoRA rank. Reconstruction improvement is greatest in early layers; CKA varies by layer and rank. The paper reports principal-angle sensitivity to subspace dimension k as small (mean angles within ±2 for k ∈ {64, 128, 256, 512}).

fits_no_version.finding: Base-model Gemma Scope SAEs reconstruct LoRA activation deltas poorly (relative error 1.13–2.46). Delta-specific SAEs reach 0.34–0.65 on held-out data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries trained on a base model do not transfer to fine-tuning-induced activation changes.

fits_no_version.finding: Over 93% of Gemma Scope features active on h∆ are not active on h_base. Delta-SAE decoder directions have a mean max cosine of about 0.071 to Gemma Scope features, and principal angles are about 74°. There is no base-base baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LoRA adapter contributions occupy feature directions geometrically separate from base-model SAE dictionaries.

record.problems: Single model, one Alpaca fine-tuning dataset, and one seed (42). The paper says the adapters' outputs were identical to the base model on test prompts, precluding causal validation by activation steering. It lacks a base-base SAE similarity baseline, and states that larger-scale SAE training may change reconstruction quality or feature vocabulary.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted Table 8 overlap and active-feature-count measures, Table 7 derived reconstruction improvements, Table 4 delta norms, and the Table 9–11 cosine, principal-angle, and CKA results. These appear in Sections 5.1 and 5.3–5.7.

untested.parts: All; no neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
All; it does not measure whether Gemma-2-9B's own activations contain SAE-recoverable sparse features or spread features across neurons.
All; no stability, canonicality or completeness test on the model's own activations. Only a single seed is used, with no base-base SAE baseline.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T3 to uses_without_test/T4. SAEs serve as the instrument, and results concern LoRA geometry and the authors' delta-SAE method. Gemma Scope's error >1 on h∆ is expected for off-distribution difference vectors (the decoder bias alone adds error), so it says nothing about dictionary completeness for the model. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks, feature sparsity transitions, regular geometry, or whether extra features are dropped.
Does not test polysemantic neurons, competition for dimensions, or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not study polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Tests SAE recovery of LoRA-induced activation deltas in Gemma-2-9B, not feature distribution across neurons in general, other LLMs, or other fine-tuning methods.
Does not test whether SAE features are stable across runs or canonical and complete units of the model's representation.
Does not compare one-dimensional features with multi-dimensional features as candidate representational units.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Adapter-specific delta SAEs, all tested ranks and layers
reader_labels.reason: Held-out reconstruction errors are 0.340–0.652 and the reported weakly aligned fractions are 0.9372–0.9968, indicating SAE-recoverable adapter-specific activation structure; recovery is incomplete (rows r25–r48, r49–r60).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Gemma Scope pretrained SAEs applied to LoRA-induced deltas, all tested ranks and layers
reader_labels.reason: Reconstruction error exceeds 1.0 in every condition, so the pretrained dictionary does not adequately recover these adapter deltas (rows r01–r24).
